title: docs(qa): state the positive secret contract and de-flake the chart measurement in platform-core (#7573, #7569)
body:
Fixes #7573
Fixes #7569

Both cards complete. The first line for #7569 was `Part of` while only the checklist half existed; the PM ruling on #7569 extended this claim's file surface to `examples/app-showcase/e2e/showcase-smoke.spec.ts`, the harness half landed in `9185685`, and the card now completes — so `Fixes` became correct.

`git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`: **2 files, +120 / -23** (56 of those lines are the checklist item file, 87 the spec; the checklist total nets out below its two commits' sum because the `knownGaps` entry added in the first commit is removed again by the second).

---

## #7573 — `platform-core.settings-hub-roundtrip` (revision 1 → 2)

The clause said only what must NOT come back. Masking, omitting `value`, and dropping the key entirely all satisfy "never returns the plaintext", and two of those three are regressions — the console renders "configured vs not configured" from exactly that field. The replacement mirrors the ten route-level pins PR #7554 added in `packages/services/service-settings/src/settings-routes.test.ts`; no vocabulary is invented here.

| 落点 | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | "…stores secrets as handles — anonymous denied" | "…stores secrets as handles **served MASKED** — anonymous denied" |
| `steps` — secret handling | **one** step: PUT a value, check the `sec_` handle in `sys_secret`, then "GET /api/settings never returns the plaintext" | **four** steps: (1) at-rest handle, unchanged; (2) the masked READ positive contract; (3) metadata survives the redaction; (4) the echoed-mask round-trip |
| `acceptance` — secret clause | one clause ending "…GET /api/settings never echoes the plaintext" | narrowed to its at-rest half (handle + ciphertext), with the read half moved into the three new clauses below |
| `acceptance` — **new** | — | set secret is served **as** the mask `••••••••`; unset stays **null** (presence-preserving); masking covers `values.< key >.value` **and every `cascadeChain` entry**; an omitted value or a vanished key is an explicit **FAIL**; both flavours (`type:'password'` and `encrypted:true`) |
| `acceptance` — **new** | — | the redaction is metadata-preserving: `source` / `locked` / `lockedReason` unchanged, so `source:'env'`, `locked:true`, the `OS_< NAMESPACE >_< KEY >` reason and the 409 `SETTINGS_LOCKED` refusal all keep working on a secret key |
| `acceptance` — **new** | — | the distinct round-trip clause the card asks for: **PUTting the echoed mask back is a NO-OP**, in both shapes (`{key: mask}` and the read-shape `{values:{key:{value: mask}}}`); a genuinely new value still writes and its PUT response is redacted too; the in-process read path is deliberately **not** masked; a non-encrypted key whose value really is the mask is written verbatim |
| `negative` | 1 secret negative | +3: omission/vanished key is a FAIL, not a pass; an echoed-mask PUT that overwrites the stored secret is a FAIL; a mask on the **in-process** path is a FAIL |
| `source` | — | +2 refs: `settings-secret-redaction.ts` and `settings-routes.test.ts` (#7522 / PR #7554) |
| `revision` / `history` | 1 | 2, with a history entry naming the negative-only → positive change |

Each of PR #7554's ten pins now has a home: the whole-body no-plaintext sweep, `value` and `cascadeChain` masking, presence-preserving null, `source`/`locked` survival, the env-locked case with its 409, both echoed-mask shapes, the real-new-secret write with a redacted response, the non-encrypted mask-verbatim control, and the in-process-plaintext guard.

## #7569 — the harness, `examples/app-showcase/e2e/showcase-smoke.spec.ts`

| 落点 | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| the settle | `await page.waitForTimeout(1500)` before every assertion | **gone** — replaced by `pollUntil` on rendered main content, bounded by the surface deadline |
| the chart box | `const box = await svg.boundingBox()`, read **once** | polled against the same deadline until non-null **and** laid out |
| collapsed-panel diagnosis | a single `not.toBeNull()` then width/height | the **last non-null** sample is retained, so a laid-out-but-collapsed chart still fails on its **width** (#2616 D) instead of reporting "no chart SVG" — different defects now read differently |
| timeout shape | a bare `waitFor` timeout | `pollUntil` returns its last sample rather than throwing, so a timeout fails as the **assertion** it belongs to, naming the surface |
| error window | `pageErrors` asserted after a fixed 1500 ms slice | asserted after the waits, so the collection window is as long as the render actually took |
| budget | two hard-coded `25_000`s plus a `1500` | one `SURFACE_BUDGET_MS`, the **source** of every deadline, sitting inside the config's 45s per-test `timeout` |

The shape is #7472 / #7409's settled spelling — loop the predicate against a deadline derived from the case's own budget, never sleep-then-read-once, with the ⛔ comment against reintroducing a fixed wall-clock wait — not a third spelling.

## #7569 — `platform-core.nav-surfaces-render` (revision 2 → 3)

| 落点 | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `acceptance[0]` clause | "…chart surfaces draw a real SVG" | "…whose box is measured by **POLLING until non-null within a bounded budget** — never by a fixed wall-clock wait followed by a single `boundingBox` read" |
| `acceptance[0]` verify | "`test:smoke` … — green" | + null-box and collapsed-panel failures now report as **different assertions** |
| `steps` | no chart-measurement step | + a chart step telling the runner the suite polls, which assertion means what, and to poll the same way when hand-walking |
| `negative` | 2 | +1: a red from a single read at a fixed instant is not a product finding — and re-introducing any sleep-then-read-once re-opens it |
| `fixtures.knownGaps` | 1 | **1** — the entry recording this harness gap was added and then removed in the same PR, because the harness half closes it |
| `revision` / `history` | 2 | 3, one entry covering both halves |

---

## Premise check (verified against `origin/main` @ `8c20f75`)

- **#7573 — premise holds.** `SETTINGS_SECRET_MASK = '••••••••'` at `settings-secret-redaction.ts:59`; the ten pins exist; the item still carried the negative-only wording.
- **#7569 — defect real, card's stated location wrong.** `showcase-smoke.spec.ts:53` was `await page.waitForTimeout(1500)` and `:66` a single `boundingBox()` read, but the card placed the fix under `docs/qa/platform-checklist/`, which holds no executable harness — only Markdown and JSON. Reported before implementing; the PM extended the surface to the spec file, and both halves are now in this PR.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit --strict` on the edited spec | ✅ exit 0 (with `--types node`; `e2e/` is **not** in the package tsconfig's `include`, so `pnpm typecheck` never covered this file — the targeted run is the real check) |
| `playwright test --list` | ✅ exit 0 — parses, all 31 surfaces enumerate |
| `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/example-showcase...' build` | ✅ exit 0 |
| `playwright test -g "Delivery Operations\|Chart Gallery\|Command Center"` | ❌ **environmental, not this change** — see below |
| `check:platform-checklist` | ❌ same single pre-existing `coverage.json · qa: UNCLASSIFIED` as the base, exit 1 — zero new problems |
| `check:nul-bytes` | ✅ OK, 7061 files |
| JSON validity | ✅ parses; both items' `revision` equals their last `history` revision |

The local smoke run cannot reach the chart assertion in this container: after shimming the missing browser build (the image ships Chromium 1194, this Playwright pins 1234), every surface times out waiting for `main` to be visible, and the page snapshot is `{"error":"Not found"}` — the container's `serve --dev` does not serve `/_console`. **Reverse-verified as environmental**: the unmodified spec restored from `HEAD` fails identically, at its own `:52` `main` waitFor, same 25s timeout, same page. So neither version reaches the chart code locally, and the `showcase-smoke` CI job is the authoritative gate — as the ruling states.

## Changeset

None — QA checklist plus an example app's e2e spec; no package behaviour and nothing user-visible to release. `skip-changeset` applied.
